blocks.raw: <Tip>Construction joints are planned weak points, not failures. They are designed to handle predictable stresses by mechanical bonding, surface roughness, and shear reinforcement. The key to success: clean the old surface (sandblast or scarify), reinforce across the joint, and keep the interface moist during new concrete placement. This is a critical supervision point for site engineers.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[ "Treating construction joints as errors or defects that should be hidden. Construction joints are intentional, designed features. They simplify scheduling and allow staged construction. Poor joints result from inadequate preparation and reinforcement, not from the joint concept itself.", "Placing construction joints without shear reinforcement (dowels or hooked bars) crossing the interface. Shear forces must be transferred; rough surface alone is insufficient in high-shear regions. Dowels are required by code at many construction joint locations.", "Neglecting surface preparation: not sandblasting or scarifying the old concrete surface before placing new concrete. The interface bond depends on mechanical interlocking with exposed aggregate; a smooth surface (laitance) will not develop adequate friction and composite action will be lost.", "Forgetting that precast members and composite structures must be tested to verify composite action and strength. Design calculations assume the two materials work together; testing confirms this assumption. Inadequate testing can lead to serviceability or strength failures." ]} />
